parole: zoning profile, zone, ZTO, description, scope, historic centre, historic net, PPE, instrument, zoning plan 2004, PRG 2004, land use plan, town plan.
domande: Which zone of the zoning plan is this point in?
What does «Scope: Historic centre» mean?
Is the plan up to date?
testo:
When you click on the map, in the **«Planning tools»** tab the section **«Zoning (zoning plan 2004)»** appears, which brings together in a single section what on the plan are several maps. The rows, when the data exists:

parole: constraints profile, area constraint, linear constraint, type, description, notes, zoning plan 2004, PRG 2004.
domande: Which constraints are there on this point?

titolo: What the Municipal property profile shows

domande: Does this building belong to the Municipality?

testo:

- **Type**.
- **Category**.
- **Address**.

parole: water district, AMAP, water, water network, district.
domande: Which water district am I in?
What is AMAP?

parole: nearby public transport, nearby stops, nearest stop, radius, as the crow flies, lines, stations.
domande: Which stops are near me?
How far does it search?
Why can't I see all the stops?
testo:
In the **«Place»** tab, after a click on the map, the section **«Nearby public transport»** appears. It lists the stops nearest to the clicked point (at most 8), with the lines that serve them in the colour of each line; stations that are opening soon are also flagged. A tap on the name takes the map to the stop.

The note says: «Stops within [radius] m as the crow flies. Tap the name to see it on the map.» If there are more stops than those listed, it adds «[n] more further away not listed». The radius is the one adjustable from the «Selection on the map» legend, the same one used by the point layers. The nearby stops are highlighted on the map as «Nearby stop», with the icon of the vehicle.

titolo: The day selector and the validity of the timetables
parole: day selector, date, valid timetables, outside validity, AMAT feed, Trenitalia feed, timetables unavailable, loading, timetable date.
domande: How do I change the day of the timetables?
Why does it show a date different from today?
Why does it say «Timetables loading…»?
testo:
In the profiles of stops and lines the timetables are downloaded only when first opened: until they arrive the profile says «Timetables loading…»; if the loading fails it says «Timetables unavailable» with the reason.

Above the timetables there is the field **«Day»**, a date selector. The initial day is today if it falls within the validity period of the feed of that stop. Otherwise the profile shows the **first valid day** and warns: «The timetables are valid from [date] to [date]: showing the first valid day.» The selector does not allow dates outside the validity period. The AMAT stops (bus and tram) and the railway stations (Trenitalia) have feeds with different periods: each stop uses its own.

titolo: The timetable profile of a stop
parole: next departures, first departures of the day, all departures of the day, arrival-only terminus, no trips, time after midnight (+1), bus times, tram times.
domande: How do I see the next departures?
Why does it say «Arrival-only terminus»?
What does «(+1)» next to the time mean?
testo:
In the profile of a stop, below the rows, there are the timetables of the chosen day:
- If the day is **today**, the **«Next departures»** block lists the next 8 departures from the current time. If there are no more it says «No more departures today.»
- If the day is **another one**, the block is called **«First departures of the day»** and shows the first 8.
- Each departure has the coloured box with the line number, the destination («→ [terminus]») and the time.
- Below there is the collapsible section **«All departures of the day (N)»**: for each line and direction, all the times in a row.
- If on that day there are no trips, it says «No trips on this date.»

The times are those of the feeds (scheduled times). A trip after midnight belongs to the previous service day and has the sign **(+1)** next to the time (for example «00:30 (+1)»). On the chosen day the trips of the previous day that arrive after midnight also appear.

An **arrival-only terminus** says so: «Arrival-only terminus: no services depart from here. Timetables are at the departure stop.» The feed has only the departures, so this is not a «no trips».

The **stations that are opening soon** have no timetables: the profile says «Station opening soon: not yet in service, so there are no timetables. It appears here because it is already in OpenStreetMap.»

titolo: The timetable profile of a line
parole: trips per day, first pass, last pass, average frequency, every N minutes, directions, line.
domande: How many trips does a line make?
What time does the first and the last one pass?
How often does it run?
testo:
When you open a line, for each direction («[from] → [to]»), a summary of the chosen day appears:
- **Trips per day**.
- **First pass at the terminus** and **Last pass at the terminus**.
- **Average frequency**: «every N min» (only if the line has more than one trip).

The summary is measured at the first stop of the line; if nothing departs from there on that day (it is the terminus of a variant) the stop of the line with the most departures is used. If there are no trips on that day it says «No trips on this date.»

When under the click there are several lines, the profile has a collapsible **list of lines**: each line has the box with the number and the name; directions and timetables are built when first opened. If there is only one line, it is already open. Opening a line (if there are several) shows it on the map.

titolo: The stops in sequence and the interchanges
parole: stops in sequence, strip diagram, interchanges, terminus, Stops (N), show the route of the line.
domande: How do I see all the stops of a line?
What are the boxes next to the name of the stop?
testo:
In each line the collapsible section **«Stops (N)»** shows the stops in sequence as a strip diagram: the line in its colour, a dot for each stop, the termini larger and in bold. Next to the name there are the coloured boxes with the number of the **other lines that serve it** (the interchanges).
- A click on the **name** of the stop: «Show the stop on the map and open its card».
- A click on the **box** of an interchange: «Show the route of line [number]», that is it takes the map to the stop and draws the route of that line («Route of line [number]»).

parole: nearby stops, distance in metres, nearest stop, lines of the stop.
domande: How far is the stop?
How do I go from the stop to its profile?
testo: In the «Nearby public transport» section each stop has the **name** (a button that takes the map to the stop and opens its profile) and the **distance in metres** (rounded to 10 metres). Below there are the boxes of its lines: a click on a box takes you to the stop and also shows the route of that line. If the station is opening soon it says so: «Opening soon: not yet in service».

parole: residents ranking, district, neighbourhood, UPL, Italians, foreigners, trend 2021-2023, residents per unit, total Palermo, population ranking, inhabitants.
domande: How do I see the inhabitants of my neighbourhood?
What does the arrow ▲ next to the number mean?
How do I switch between districts, neighbourhoods and UPL?
testo:
In the «Census section» profile («Population» tab) there is a **ranking of residents** titled «Resident population by [level]». At the top three buttons choose the level: **District**, **Neighbourhoods**, **UPL** (the one chosen is kept even when you reopen the profile).

The list is ordered from the most populous. Each row has: position, name, a bar divided into **Italians** and **foreigners**, the number of residents, the percentage of foreigners and a **trend badge 2021→2023**: ▲ growth, ▼ decline, ≈ stable (change below 0.5%), with the percentage. Hovering over the badge you read «2021: [n] → 2023: [n]». Hovering over a row you read total, Italians, foreigners and percentage of foreigners. The unit in which the clicked point falls is highlighted and brought into view in the list.

At the bottom there is the total «Palermo — total» with the residents, the foreigners (for.) and their percentage, with the trend. Source written in the profile: ISTAT, Permanent Census 2021, census sections; trend: 2023 update, AGID Cruscotto Italia (dati.gov.it).

parole: trend chart, inhabitants 2011 2021 2023, scenario 2030 2035, uncertainty band, solid line, dashed line, trend scenario, population projection.
domande: How do I read the chart?
What does the dashed line mean?
What is the coloured area?
testo:
For each level (UPL, Neighbourhood, District) the profile has a collapsible section, «[Level]: [name]» (the first is open), with a chart:
- **Solid line** with the observed points ’11, ’21 and ’23 (filled circles).
- **Dashed line** with the scenario ’30 and ’35 (empty circles) and a **coloured area** that is the uncertainty band between minimum and maximum.
- The number of inhabitants is written on each point (below the point for 2023).
- The colour follows the change 2011-2021: green growth, purple decline.

Below the chart: «Trend scenario to 2035: [central value] ([minimum]–[maximum])». At the bottom the collapsible section «Note on data quality», closed at the start, with the caution on the comparison between the censuses.

parole: lives and works here, works elsewhere, jobs filled by commuters, working population, jobs, net balance, top destinations, top origins, show all links, commuting rankings.
domande: What do the three boxes mean?
What is the net balance?
Why are there only 25 municipalities?
testo:
The drawn part of the «Commuting for work» profile has:
- **Three percentage boxes**: «Lives and works here», «Works elsewhere» and «Jobs filled by commuters».
- **Three key figures**: «Working population», «Jobs» and «Net balance» (with the sign + or −, highlighted differently if positive or negative).
- A hint: «The map shows the top 25 links per direction (share of at least 1%). Turn on “Show all links” in the legend to see them all.»
- Two rankings with bars: **«Top destinations (outbound)»** and **«Top origins (inbound)»**, with municipality, number of people and share of the direction.
- The collapsible section «Note on data quality» (data at 31 December 2021 in the middle of the pandemic; municipalities at the centroid, arcs are not real routes).

parole: charging points occupied now, charging, total charging points, active, inactive, in use, active real, active estimated, monitorable, gauge, electric vehicle charging.
domande: How many charging points are in use right now?
What does «Active (estimated)» mean?
Why is the percentage calculated only on some charging points?
testo:
Above the list of charging points, in the profile, there are two charts on **all the charging points of the Municipality**.

**«Charging points occupied now»**: a semicircle gauge with the percentage and the number «N charging». The note says: «[N] vehicles charging at this moment ([percentage]% of the [M] charging points where monitoring is possible).» The **monitorable** charging points are the active ones with real-time status; the percentage is calculated only on these.

**«Total charging points»**: the total number and two bars.
- The first divides the charging points into **Active** and **Inactive**.
- The second, «of which active», divides them into **In use** (charging), **Active (real)** (real-time status) and **Active (estimated)** (estimated status only).
- Below, the legend with the numbers and the note: «Not all charging points can be monitored: “in use” is only shown for those with real-time status.»

Hovering over a segment of the bar you read the number and the percentage.

titolo: Chart of the trend of the heat islands
parole: heat islands chart, trend 2019-2025, city average, quartiles, section, surface temperature, band.
domande: How do I read the heat islands chart?
What are the quartiles?
testo:
The line chart shows the trend of the summer surface temperature from 2019 to 2025:
- **Section** (solid orange line, with a point for each year): the temperature of the clicked section. Hovering over a point you read «[year]: [value] °C». The years without data leave a gap.
- **City average** (dashed grey line).
- **City quartiles (25th–75th)**: the light grey band around the city average.

Without a clicked section (in the legend of the layer) the chart shows only the city trend. The vertical axis is in degrees °C. The description for screen readers also gives all the values.

titolo: Interactive parts of the PEBA profile
parole: score bar, issues found, survey photos, photo viewer, save photo, rotate photo, note on data quality, accessibility plan.
domande: How do I see the photos of a survey?
Can I save them?
What does the bar say?
testo:
Below the rows of the PEBA profile there appear, when the data is there:
- **Score bar**: as long as the inaccessibility score (0-100), in the colour of the level. For those who use a screen reader it says «Inaccessibility score [n] out of 100».
- **«Issues found»**: the bulleted list of the issues found.
- **«Survey photos (N)»**: a grid of thumbnails. If a thumbnail is not there, the profile tries the large photo from the PEBA website; if that is missing too, the box disappears.
- **«Note on data quality»**: collapsible section, closed at the start, which warns that profiles, texts and photos were extracted automatically and the coordinates derive from the geocoding of the addresses.

A click on a thumbnail (a normal click, without Ctrl, Shift or Cmd) opens the **«Survey photos» viewer**. The controls of the viewer are: **Previous photo**, **Next photo**, **Rotate left**, **Rotate right**, **Save photo** and **Close**. With Ctrl, Cmd or Shift the thumbnail behaves like a normal browser link to the large photo.

parole: profile header, coordinates, district, neighbourhood, UPL, profile title, place profile, tabs.
domande: Where do I see the coordinates of the point?
How do I know which neighbourhood I am in?
Why does the profile title change?

titolo: Profile controls: copy, print, customise, close
parole: copy address, cadastral references, print the profile, customise the information, close the profile, Esc.
domande: How do I copy the address and the parcel?
How do I print the profile?
How do I hide information I do not need?
testo:
At the top right of the profile there are four buttons:
- **Copy address and cadastral references**: copies the address and «Sheet [n], parcel [n]» to the clipboard. The button shows «Copied» for a moment.
- **Print the profile**: the printout includes an extract of the map as displayed.
- **Customise the information**: opens the «Customise» panel.
- **Close the profile** (also with Esc).

The **Customise** panel lets you choose which topics to show in the profiles: there is the «Search topic…» field, and the «Select all» and «Deselect all» buttons. The choices are saved in this browser; if the browser does not save them, they hold as long as the page stays open. **Warning:** the choice does not turn the layer on the map on, only the information in the profile; the layer has to be turned on by hand. If all the information is hidden the profile says: «All the information in this profile is hidden: open «Customise» to show it.»

titolo: Layer switch, missing data and classes from 1 to 5
parole: show the layer on the map, hide the layer, no data at this point, not available, class out of 5, no data.
domande: Why does the profile say «No data at this point»?
What does «Class 3 of 5» mean?
testo:
- Each section of the profile has a switch, **«Show the layer on the map»** / **«Hide the layer from the map»**, to turn the layer of that topic on or off.
- If there is no data at the point the profile says «No data at this point: zoom in or turn on a layer.»
- When several rows of a section have no data, they are gathered in a single row «Not available: [list]».
- Rows with a judgement in classes (for example stability and buildability of the ground) show «Class [n] of 5 (1 = best)».
- Sections marked as informational carry the note «Informational data, with no legal value: for legal use, land-registry extracts and a certificate of planning use are required.»

titolo: The disclaimer at the bottom of the profile
parole: disclaimer, legal notice, legal value, SISTER, certificate of planning use, sample-based estimates.
domande: What does the notice at the bottom of the profile say?
testo: At the bottom of every profile there is the notice: «The Digital Twin is a tool for learning, studying and understanding the city. It does not replace official documents. Cadastre, zoning plan and constraints are purely informational here and have no legal value. For a land-registry extract or a certificate of planning use, contact SISTER or the competent offices. Population data for individual buildings are also sample-based estimates and should be read as indications, not exact counts.»

parole: theme, interface theme, change the colours, dark theme, light theme, customise, ready-made themes, Theme tab, right-hand bar, colour scheme, appearance.
domande: How do I change the colours of the site?
Where is the dark theme?
Does my theme stay saved?
How do I go back to the original colours?
testo:
The **«Interface theme»** panel opens from the **Theme** tab of the right-hand bar (next to Profile, RNDT and Geoimage). It changes the colours and the text of **the whole application**, not just the map. Every choice has an **instant preview**. At the top there is a status line: «Pick a ready-made theme or adjust the colours: the preview is instant.»; after a choice it says «Active theme: [name]. It stays saved in this browser.» or «Custom theme active; it stays saved in this browser.»

The panel has four sections: **Ready-made themes**, **Colours**, **Text** and **File on your computer**. The button with the moon in the toolbar is another route: it switches from the light theme to the dark theme and, if there was a custom theme, removes it and goes back to the standard colours.

parole: ready-made themes, light, dark, accessibility, high contrast, colour-blind, show more, Sea, Forest, Sepia, Midnight blue, Terminal.
domande: Which themes are there?
Is there a theme for colour-blind users?
Is there a high-contrast theme?
testo:
The ready-made themes have a thumbnail and are divided into three groups:
- **Light**: Light, Sea, Forest, Sepia, Lavender, Grey, Paper, Mint, Dusty rose, Dawn.
- **Dark**: Dark, Midnight blue, Sunset, Graphite, Ocean, Purple night, Terminal.
- **Accessibility**: **High contrast**, **Colour-blind: red-green** (for those who confuse red with green) and **Colour-blind: blue-yellow** (for those who confuse blue with yellow). These three are always all in view.

In the Light and Dark groups the first four themes are shown; the «Show [n] more» button shows the others and «Show fewer» closes them again. The active theme is marked; if it is among the hidden ones the group opens by itself. One click on a theme applies it immediately.

The two colour-blind themes use a palette designed for this purpose and also change the colours for success, error, notices, the searched parcel and the values in charts, which are no longer green and red.

parole: background, text, accent, links, borders and lines, hexadecimal, contrast, fix, advanced colours, success, error and alarm, notice background, searched parcel, chart values.
domande: How do I choose an exact colour?
What does the contrast notice mean?
What are the advanced colours for?
testo:
The **«Colours»** section has a live preview (a thumbnail of the interface) and five basic colours:
**Background**, **Text**, **Accent**, **Links** and **Borders and lines**.

Each colour is chosen with the browser's colour picker or by typing the **hexadecimal code** (with or without #). As long as the code is not valid the field marks the error and the theme does not change.

**Contrast check.** For **Text** and **Links** the app measures the contrast with the background. If it is too low the notice «Contrast [n]:1 on the background: at least 4.5:1 is needed to read comfortably.» appears, with the **«Fix»** button, which brings the colour to the nearest one that reaches the minimum.

**Advanced colours** (collapsible section «Advanced colours»): status and highlight colours. If you do not choose them, they use the standard ones of the light or dark theme. There are five:
- **Success**: confirmation messages and active switches.
- **Error and alarm**: errors, alarms and actions that delete.
- **Notice background**: the background of the yellow banners.
- **Searched parcel**: the outline of the cadastral parcel searched for.
- **Chart values**: bars and lines of the charts in the profiles.

The «Reset advanced colours» button appears only if you have changed any of them. From the five basic colours the app works out the others by itself (secondary backgrounds, muted text, borders, highlighting, speech bubbles).

If the background colour chosen is dark, the app also automatically switches the light/dark button (logo, base map and header) to match the theme.

parole: text size, enlarge the text, typeface, font, Montserrat, Georgia, Atkinson Hyperlegible, high legibility, monospace, reading difficulty.
domande: How do I enlarge the text?
Can I change the typeface?
Is there a typeface for people with reading difficulties?
testo:
The **«Text»** section has:
- **Text size**: a slider from **85% to 150%**, in steps of 5%. 100% is the default and the slider scales the whole interface.
- **Typeface**: **Montserrat (default)**, **System font**, **Serif (Georgia)**, **Monospace** and **Atkinson Hyperlegible (high legibility)**.
- A preview («Palermo Digital Twin: 0123456789 — Text preview»).
- The **«Reset standard text»** button, active only if something differs from the default.

titolo: Saving, loading and resetting the theme
parole: save to file, load from file, JSON file, restore standard colours, undo, another device, theme privacy.
domande: Is the theme sent to anyone?
How do I use it on another device?
How do I remove it?
Can I go back if I remove it by mistake?
testo:
The **«File on your computer»** section has:
- **Save to file**: saves the theme to a `.json` file on the computer (the suggested name is `tema-digital-twin.json`; where the browser allows it, a «Save as» window opens).
- **Load from file**: reads a theme from a `.json` file. If the file is not a JSON, is not an interface theme or does not contain valid colours, the app reports it.
- **Restore standard colours**: removes the custom theme and goes back to the colours of the app.

The note says: «The theme is saved to a file on your computer: it is not sent to anyone. You can load it back here or on another device.» The active theme also stays **saved in the browser** and is found again on the next visit; if the browser cannot save it, it holds for the session.

After removing the custom theme (with «Restore standard colours» or with the light/dark switch) the **«Undo»** button appears for about eight seconds to get it back.

titolo: Colouring a layer: fill, outline, width
parole: layer colours, palette, fill, outline, width, colour by category, reset, export JSON, import JSON.
domande: How do I change the colour of a layer?
How do I go back to the original style?
How do I share the colours of a layer?
testo:
Next to each layer the **palette** button («Colours of [layer name]») opens a small panel (it appears only if the layer has polygons, points or lines). It contains, when needed:
- **Fill** and **Outline** (colour); for lines **Line colour** and **Width** (slider from 0 to 6, in steps of 0.5).
- **Colours by category**: one colour for each category of the layer; the dots in the legends follow the colour chosen.
- **Colour by attribute** (see below).
- **Reset** (goes back to the original style: «Original style restored»), **Export JSON** (exports the themes of all layers) and **Import JSON**.

The theme of each layer is saved in the browser. If the file imported is not valid, the app reports it («Invalid file: not a JSON file», «Invalid file: not a layer theme» or «The file contains no valid themes»).

titolo: Colour by attribute: categories and graduated
parole: colour by attribute, by category, graduated, quantiles, equal intervals, ramp, ColorBrewer, Crameri, reverse the colour scale, detect values, field, classes, theme legend, choropleth.
domande: How do I colour the buildings by density?
What are quantiles and equal intervals?
What does «Detect values» mean?
What are the Crameri ramps?
testo:
In the small colour panel the **«Colour by attribute»** section colours the features according to a field of the data. You choose:
- **Type**: **None**, **By category** (one colour for each value of the field) or **Graduated (numeric)** (divides a numeric field into classes).
- **Field**: the data field. The **«Detect values»** button reads the values of the features that are in view; if no feature is in view the app says to turn on the layer and frame the area, then press «Detect values».
- For the graduated type: **Method** (**Quantiles**, the same number of features per class, or **Equal intervals**) and **Classes** (up to nine; if the values are too similar to form classes it says so).
- **Ramp**: the colours. Groups: **ColorBrewer** (Blue, Green, Orange, Purple, Red–Green), **Crameri · sequential** (Batlow, Acton, Bamako, Bilbao, Davos, Devon, Lajolla, Lapaz, Oslo, Tokyo, Turku) and **Crameri · diverging** (Bam, Broc, Cork, Roma, Vik), which need «a reference value». Crameri's scales are perceptually uniform and also suited to colour blindness.
- **Reverse the colour scale**: reads the ramp from the other end.

For categories, with over 200 distinct values the app suggests another field or the graduated type. On the map, at the bottom left, the **theme legend** appears when the layer is on; for layers with a built-in legend only the colours of the legend change.

parole: layers in 3D, stack, separate layers, explode, 3D view of the layers, in development, beta, overlapping layers, 3D layers.
domande: What does the «Layers in 3D» button do?
Can I see the layers separately, one above the other?
Why is it «In development»?
testo:
«Layers in 3D» takes the layers that are **on** in the map, "photographs" them one by one in the current view and separates them into a **stack** of overlapping planes, which you turn with the mouse or with a finger. The images come from the map itself: styles, filters and colours are those of the app. The feature carries the label **«In development»**: «Feature in development: it may change and have some rough edges».

The «Layers in 3D» button is in the toolbar (on a smartphone, in the «Layers» sheet). It is off until at least one layer is on; in that case the tooltip says «Turn on at least one layer to see it in 3D». While it prepares the stack, «Preparing the 3D layers… [n] of [tot]» appears. If something goes wrong it says «The 3D layer view did not open: try again».

titolo: Which layers end up in the stack
parole: planes, maximum number of layers, too many layers on, 3D terrain, base map, other layers.
domande: Why do I not see all my layers?
How many layers can I put in?
What are «Base map» and «Other layers»?
testo:
- One plane for each **layer that is on**, in the drawing order of the map (the first is at the bottom).
- The **base map** is always under everything.
- **«Other layers»**: the visible layers that do not belong to a module of the app, such as those from the RNDT catalogue, from «My layers» or the maps added.
- The **3D relief** and the **elevation** become a single **«3D terrain»** plane at the bottom of the stack, because the coloured elevation has to rest on the relief.
- A plane with nothing to show (a layer outside the view, a service layer) does not enter the stack.

**Limit**: at most **14 planes on a computer and 8 on a smartphone**. If more layers are on, the base, the terrain and those highest in the drawing order remain, and the app warns: «Too many active layers: the 3D view shows the top [n]».

titolo: The «Layers in 3D» screen: list and controls
parole: stack list, eye, hide in the stack, explode, rotate, from above, in 3D, back to the map, point profile.
domande: How do I hide a layer in the stack?
What do Explode, Rotate and From above do?
How do I go back to the map?
testo:
When the screen opens, the stack rises above the map at the same scale (it looks as if the map itself lifts up). At the top there are the title «Layers in 3D», the «In development» label and the **«Back to the map»** button. You can also leave with **Esc**.

**List of the layers in the stack**: a row of numbered chips, with the last layer at the top as in the stack. Each chip has:
- an **eye** to hide or show the layer **only in the stack** («Hide [name] in the stack» / «Show [name] in the stack again»); while the screen is open a hidden layer is also hidden on the map underneath, so it gives neither a speech bubble nor a profile; on closing it goes back as it was;
- the **name**: one click highlights it.

**Controls** under the list:
- **Explode**: a slider that adjusts the distance between the planes (from 0 to 1.6; it starts at 1).
- **Rotate**: turns the automatic rotation on or off. It starts on, unless the system asks to reduce animations; it stops when you use the stack and resumes after about two and a half seconds without gestures.
- **From above** / **In 3D**: brings the stack to a view from above (flat) and then tilted again; the button changes name accordingly.
- **Step between layers** / **Leave the stack**: see below.

At the bottom the tooltip appears: «Drag to turn, scroll to zoom, right-click to move. Or use the compass and joystick at the bottom left, or the W A S D keys. Press ? for the guide.» The **«How to move» guide** opens by itself only the first time; after that you call it up with the «How to move (?)» button or with the ? key. It closes with «Got it» or Esc.

titolo: Profile and speech bubbles inside the stack
parole: click on a point, profile inside the stack, tooltip, edge of a layer, pin, everything under a point.
domande: Can I open the profile of a point from the stack?
What do I see when I hover with the mouse?
How do I choose a layer?
testo:
- A **click on a point** of a layer opens the profile of that point, above the scene, staying in 3D. The layers are queried in order: the one touched, then those below, then those above. The profile opens on the tab of the layer touched.
- A **click on the edge of a layer** chooses it («[name]: click to pick it, again to step in (from inside: to go there)»).
- On the point clicked a **pin** appears that crosses the stack, with a dot on each layer.
- When you hover with the mouse a **speech bubble** appears as on the 2D map, with the same tooltip templates of the app: for each layer that has something at that point, the title and the attributes. It shows at most 3 items per layer and then «+ [n] more». The layer under the mouse is on top and highlighted. For cadastral parcels it writes «Sheet [n], parcel [n]».

parole: step between layers, gap, walk, on the layer, look up, look down, go down one layer, go up one layer, Page Up Page Down.
domande: What does «Step between layers» mean?
How do I move from one layer to another?
How do I walk on the layer?
testo:
With **«Step between layers»** the eye goes into a **gap** between two planes and you can look down, up and around. The label says where you are: «Between [layer below] and [layer above]».

Controls from inside:
- **Go down one layer** / **Go up one layer** (also Page Down and Page Up).
- **Look down** / **Look up**.
- **Walk**: «Walk on the layer below you, looking ahead». You stand on the plane («On layer [n]») and with the controls **Go down to the layer below** / **Go up to the layer above** you change plane.
- The Esc key or **«Leave the stack»** take you back out.

The app's tooltips: «You are between two layers: drag sideways to turn the model, up or down to look above or below. Joystick or W/S to move, scroll to zoom, Page Up and Page Down to change gap.» and, while walking: «You are walking on the layer: hold W/S (or the joystick) to go forward and back, A/D to turn, Q/E to side-step. Drag to look around, scroll to zoom.»

parole: 3D controls, W A S D, wheel, right button, compass, joystick, zoom, tilt, touch, two fingers.
domande: Which keys do I use to move?
How do I move the stack?
How do I use 3D on a phone?
testo:
**Mouse**
- Drag: turns the model; while walking, you look around.
- Right button, or Shift + drag: move.
- Wheel: zoom; from inside, backwards until you leave.
- Click on a point: its profile; on the edge of a layer: chooses it.

**Keyboard**
- W S or ↑ ↓: forward and back, while held.
- A D or ← →: turn; Q E: side-step.
- R F or Shift + ↑ ↓: tilt; + and −: zoom.
- Page Up / Page Down: layer above or below; ? guide; Esc leaves.

**Touch and navigator**
- One finger turns; two fingers zoom and move.
- **Compass** (bottom left): drag the ring to turn, one click goes back to north.
- **Joystick**: drag the knob to move, the farther from the centre the faster.
- **+ / −** buttons (zoom in and out) and tilt up/down: hold them down. «Back to the centre» resets the view. «How to move (?)» opens the guide.

titolo: The 3D view of the map («3D view» button)
parole: 3D view, tilt the map, 3D navigator, compass, joystick, W A S D, Q E, R F, right button.
domande: How do I tilt the map?
What changes with the 3D view?
How do I move?
testo:
The **«3D view»** button in the toolbar tilts the real map (not the stack). Only in this view does the **navigator** appear at the bottom left, with compass, joystick, zoom and tilt, the same as in the stack. The tilt goes up to 65°.

Controls of the guide «How to move in the 3D view»:
- **Mouse**: dragging moves the map; right button + drag rotates and tilts; wheel zooms; a click on a feature opens its profile.
- **Keyboard**: W A S D move the map, while held; Q E turn left and right; R F tilt; + and − zoom; ? opens the guide, Esc closes it.
- **Touch**: one finger moves; two fingers zoom, rotate and tilt; compass and joystick as above.

In 3D view the **«3D buildings»** layer extrudes the buildings and the **3D relief** shows the terrain (see `03-edifici-e-popolazione.md` and `02-territorio-e-urbanistica.md`).

titolo: The layers in 3D on the presentation page
parole: 3D presentation, all the layers in 3D, fifteen layers, demonstration model.
domande: Is there a demo of the layers in 3D?
Where do I find it?
testo: The **Presentation** page of the menu has a section «All the layers, in 3D»: «The map's fifteen layers, pulled apart one above the other: turn them with the mouse or a finger, tap a layer in the list to highlight it. In the app you do it with your own active layers, from the «Layers in 3D» button.» It has the controls Explode, Rotate, From above / In 3D, Zoom in and Zoom out. Dragging turns it, the wheel with Ctrl zooms, the keyboard arrows rotate and tilt. It needs JavaScript.

titolo: What the data table is and how to open it
parole: data table, attribute table, rows, columns, drawer, layer on, features in view, open the table.
domande: Where do I see the data of a layer as a table?
Why is the table empty?
Which rows does it show?
testo:
The **«Data table»** button in the toolbar (on a smartphone, in the «Layers» sheet) opens from the bottom a drawer with the rows of the layers that are on, in the style of an attribute table. Each layer that is on has its own tab. The table reads **only the features loaded in the current view**: as you move or zoom the map it updates (after a short pause from the movement). This is why the app warns «Only the features loaded in view.»

Messages when there is nothing to show:
- «No layer is on: turn one on to see its rows.»
- «No features in view. Turn on a layer from the card and zoom in.»

**Height of the drawer**: it is changed by dragging the handle «Resize the table» (also with the keyboard); the height chosen stays saved in the browser (at the start 280 px). It closes with «Close the table».

titolo: Which layers can be seen in the table
parole: layers in the table, which layers, list of table layers, added layers, PAI.
domande: Does my layer have a table?
Which layers are there?
testo:
The table knows these layers: Charging stations, Fuel stations, Schools and nurseries, Municipal offices, Public transport stops, Cadastre: parcels, Road accidents, Districts (circoscrizioni), Neighbourhoods, UPL, AMAP water districts, Census sections, Monuments, Monumental trees, Public drinking fountains, Polling stations, Municipal properties, Accidents per km on roads, The 20 most dangerous roads, Accident hotspots, Bus lines, Tram lines, Wildfires, House numbers, OMI zones 2025, PRG 2004 (zoning, historic centre PPE, area constraints, line constraints), Heat islands, Properties declared to the MEF, PEBA, PNRR, Public works, Commuting to and from Palermo 2021 and Population by section. There are also the **PAI themes** (registered at start-up) and the **layers you added** (file, WFS, ArcGIS, RNDT): for these the source is «Layer you added: source and licence are those of the original file or service».

For each layer the table starts with the **main columns** (for example, for the cadastre, sheet and parcel); the other fields are in the «Columns» menu.

titolo: Filtering, sorting and choosing the columns
parole: filter the rows, sort, columns, show the column, move column, export the column, header.
domande: How do I search for a text in the table?
How do I sort by a column?
How do I hide or reorder the columns?
testo:
- **«Filter the rows»**: searches the text in all the fields of the row.
- **Sorting**: one click on the header («Sort by [column]»). Numbers are sorted as numbers, text in Italian alphabetical order; empty cells stay at the bottom in both directions.
- **«Columns» menu**: for each column there are the checkbox «Show the column [name]», the checkbox «Export the column [name]» and the arrows ◀ ▶ to move it left or right. Hiding a column also removes it from the exported file; showing it again puts it back; the «Export» checkbox on its own acts only on the export.
- The choices about the columns are saved in the browser **for each layer**.
- When new fields appear as the view moves, they are added at the end.
- Cells with lists (arrays) are shown separated by semicolons.

**Limits**: if there are more than **20,000** rows the table asks you to narrow the view or the selection («More than 20000 rows»). On the page at most **2,000** rows are shown («Showing the first 2000 rows: filter or narrow down to see the others»).

parole: selection, click, box, polygon, area, district, neighbourhood, UPL, back to the view, clear the selection, select all rows, invert.
domande: How do I select only the features inside an area?
How do I draw a polygon?
How do I add to the selection?
testo:
The four **selection tools** are in the bar of the table. When one is active the cursor becomes a crosshair; it is switched off by pressing the button again or with **Esc**.
- **Click**: chooses the feature under the click (tolerance of about 6 pixels).
- **Box**: you drag a rectangle (a drag that is too short is ignored). While dragging, the map does not move.
- **Polygon**: one click for each vertex, a **double click** closes the shape. At least 3 distinct vertices are needed, otherwise it says «At least 3 distinct vertices are needed.»
- **Area**: a click inside a district, a neighbourhood or a UPL; the «Area type» menu chooses which. If there is no area under the click it says «No area under the click: turn on the boundaries and try again.»

Holding down **Ctrl (or Cmd)** during the click, the new choice is **added** to the previous one. With a selection active the table shows only the rows that fall in the areas chosen; **«Back to the view»** returns to the rows visible on the map. On a smartphone the Box and Polygon tools are hidden.

Single rows are ticked with the row checkbox; with **Shift** a range is ticked. There are «Select all rows», **Invert** and «Clear the selection». An announcement for screen readers says how many rows are selected.

parole: export, CSV, GeoJSON, download, rows × columns, exported file, source and licence, approximate geometry, confirmation, file name.
domande: How do I download the data?
What does the file contain?
Why does the GeoJSON ask for confirmation?
Can I export all the layers?
testo:
The **«CSV»** and **«GeoJSON»** buttons show how many rows and columns will come out (for example «33 × 15»). The **selected rows** come out; if none is selected, **all the rows of the table** come out. The columns with the «Export» checkbox active come out. The button is off if there are no rows or columns.

**All the layers listed have export enabled**, including those you added. If it were not enabled for a layer the button says «Export is not enabled for this layer yet.» (For third-party layers the licence conditions of the source apply, indicated in the file.)

- **CSV**: the first row has the original names of the fields (not the translated labels, so they stay the same in all languages); comma separator; the last column **«fonte»** (the name is in Italian in the file) gives the source and licence of the layer. The file begins with a marker that lets Excel read accented letters correctly.
- **GeoJSON**: a FeatureCollection with the properties of the columns chosen and the geometry of each row. A `metadata` block gives the layer, the source, whether the geometry is approximate and the date of the export.
- **Simplified geometry**: for some layers the geometry already arrives simplified by the tiles (cadastre, accidents, boundaries and sections, municipal properties, road safety, wildfires, OMI, PRG and constraints, heat islands, population by section, layers you added). The table warns «Geometry simplified by the tiles: use the CSV for exact data.» and, before exporting the GeoJSON, asks «This layer has geometry simplified by the tiles. Export the GeoJSON anyway?» When a feature is cut by the tiles into several pieces, the row still has a single merged geometry.
- **File name**: `[layer]-YYYY-MM-DD.csv` or `.geojson`.

Commuting uses the whole file (not just what is in view) and the CUP link columns of PNRR and public works point to OpenCUP.

parole: Street View, pegman, little man, panorama, Google Maps, blue cone, viewing direction, window, street at eye level, Google account.
domande: How do I see a street at eye level?
How do I choose the direction?
Why is the window empty?
Do I need a Google account?
testo:
The button with the little man (**«Street View: press a point and drag to pick the direction»**) is in the toolbar at the top right. Once pressed, the tool is active: the button appears pressed, the cursor becomes a **crosshair** and the map no longer moves when dragged. The tooltip becomes «Street View on: press a point and drag, Esc to exit».

**How to use it**
1. You **press** on the point of the map that interests you (mouse or finger).
2. **Keeping it pressed**, you drag to choose the direction of the view: a **blue cone** 90° wide appears, showing where the panorama will look. The direction takes into account any rotation of the map.
3. On **release** the window with the panorama opens.

If the drag is less than about 6 pixels it is a simple click: the panorama opens without a direction chosen (it looks north). With two fingers on the screen the gesture does not start.

**The window**
- It is a floating, non-modal window: the map stays visible.
- It is **moved** by dragging the bar at the top and **resized** from the corner. It remembers its position for the next opening.
- It contains the Google Street View panorama of the point. The **«Open in Google Maps ↗»** link in the bar opens it full screen in a new tab; the **✕** button («Close») closes it. Opening a new panorama closes the previous one.
- No API key and no Google account is needed.

**Leaving the tool**: **Esc** or a new click on the button. The cone and the point disappear and the map can be dragged again.

**Limits**: where Google has no images the window stays empty or shows the nearest panorama. The panorama is an external Google service and is not part of the map data: when it opens, the browser contacts Google's servers (see `51-pagine-privacy-lingua-e-offline.md`).

parole: print, print the map, A4 A3 A2 A1 A0 format, landscape, portrait, scale 1:1,000, current view, scale bar, legend, sources and attributions, PDF, paper size, printout.
domande: How do I print the map?
Which formats are there?
How do I print to scale?
What does the sheet contain?
testo:
The button with the printer (**«Print the current map»**) in the toolbar opens a small menu with four choices:
- **Scale**: «Current view (no scale)» or a fixed scale: **1:1,000, 1:2,000, 1:5,000, 1:10,000, 1:25,000**.
- **Format**: **A4, A3, A2, A1, A0**.
- **Orientation**: **Landscape** or **Portrait**.
- The **Print** button (disabled while it prepares the image).

The menu closes with **Esc** or by clicking outside. The browser then opens the print window, from which you can also save to PDF.

**What the sheet contains**
- The title **«Palermo Digital Twin»** and a line with the date, the **centre of the map** (latitude and longitude) and, depending on the case, «scale 1:[n]» or «zoom [n]».
- The **image of the map** you are looking at, with all the layers that are on.
- With a fixed scale, the **scale bar** in metres or kilometres and the note: «[length] · scale 1:[n] (print at 100%, without fitting to the page)».
- The **«Legend»**, only for the layers that are on (hidden or empty legends are not printed).
- **«Sources and attributions»**: the attributions of the maps, without repetitions.

**Current view or fixed scale.** With the «Current view» the map is printed as it is. With a fixed scale the app takes the map, out of sight, to the size of the print frame and to the zoom matching the scale (with rotation and tilt reset, seen from above), waits for the tiles to arrive (at most 12 seconds), captures the image and puts the map back as it was. The centre stays that of the view.

**Dimensions.** The sheet has 10 mm margins and reserves about 65 mm below the map for the title, scale, legend and sources. For each format the resolution is 192 dpi; for A0 it is reduced (96 dpi) so as not to exceed the browser's limits, and it is reduced further if the graphics card cannot handle large sizes.

**To really print to scale** the sheet must be printed at 100%, without «fit to page».

parole: print the profile, extract of the map, print the data of a point, place profile, print a point.
domande: Can I print the profile of a point?
What is on the sheet?
testo: The **«Print the profile»** button in the header of the place profile prints the profile. At the top of the sheet an **extract of the displayed map** («Extract of the displayed map») is added, with a circle on the point that was clicked. If the map image cannot be read, it is printed without the extract. After printing, the profile goes back to how it was.

titolo: What the «Share this view» button does
parole: share, link, share the map, copy link, WhatsApp, Telegram, Facebook, X, LinkedIn, email, shared view, send the map, URL.
domande: How do I send someone my view?
What does the link contain?
Can I share on social media?
testo:
The **«Share this view»** button in the toolbar opens a window with the **link to the current view**. The field with the link is already selected. The controls:
- **Copy**: copies the link to the clipboard. The button says «Copied» for a moment; if the browser does not allow direct copying it says «Select and copy».
- **Share…**: appears only on devices whose browser has the native share menu.
- The icons to share the link on **WhatsApp, Telegram, Facebook, X, LinkedIn** and to send it by **Email** («Share on [network]»). The suggested text is «Palermo Digital Twin: my map view».

It closes with the X, with **Esc** or by clicking outside. Whoever opens the link sees the same view.
