domande: Does the link keep the layers that are on?
Why does my layer not appear for whoever receives the link?
What does «The view is very rich» mean?

parole: link to the profile, clicked point, shared profile, profile tab, profile parameter.
domande: If I share the link with the profile open, does whoever receives it see it?
Does the chosen tab stay?
testo: When the place profile is opened, the browser address is updated with the clicked point and the chosen tab. When a link that contains a profile point is opened, the app, after the first loading of the data, **reopens the profile at that point** (and on the tab indicated).

parole: search, find, search bar, street, street number, address, places, results, no results, marker, house number, look up an address.
domande: What can I search for?
How do I search for a street with the street number?
How do the results work?
testo:
The search field is at the bottom of the map (on a smartphone at the top, under the logo). The search starts when at least **3 characters** (or a number) are typed. The results appear in a list under the field. You choose a result with a click or with **Enter**, which takes the first one. The map flies to the point (zoom 18 unless indicated otherwise), a **marker** appears on the point and the text of the result goes into the field. If the result is a place of a layer that is off, the layer turns on by itself. Clicking outside the bar closes the list. If there is nothing: «No results».

**What can be found**
- **Streets and street numbers**: you write the name of the street, all the words in any order, and if needed the number. With «street + number» the search goes to the exact street number; for a number with a letter (for example 4A) it must be written with the letter. If you write “4” and only 4A, 4B… exist, it proposes them. If the street number does not exist, it goes to the street with the note “civico non trovato” (street number not found). Accents and capital letters are ignored. The street numbers are those of the Municipality of Palermo.
- **Places by name**: schools and nurseries, polling stations (also by section number), monuments, monumental trees, drinking fountains, stops (with the lines), bus and tram lines (by number or name), stations and lines of the urban railway, charging points, fuel stations, municipal offices, municipal properties and MEF properties, PEBA, PNRR projects and public works.
- **Cadastral parcels**: you write “12/345”, “f 12 p 345” or “foglio 12 particella 345”. The result is “Cadastral parcel — sheet [n], parcel [n]”.
- **Neighbourhoods, districts and UPL**: the areas whose name starts with the text appear first.
- **Fires and PAI constraints**: see below.
- **Road accidents and streets**: see below.
- **Guide topics**: the search proposes up to 3 guide topics (Guide, Geoimage guide, RNDT plugin), each with the name of the guide.

**Order of the results**: first the rows about accidents (if “incidente” was written), then the areas that start with the text, the places by name, the streets and street numbers and, at the bottom, the areas that contain the text and the rows about streets with accidents.

If an archive does not load, the search says so («Search unavailable: [reason]», «street-number index unavailable»).

titolo: Searching for accidents and dangerous streets
parole: accident, crash, fatal accident, accidents on a street, year, severity, dangerous road, road safety, most dangerous streets.
domande: How do I find the accidents on a street?
How do I search only for fatal ones?
Can I search by year?
testo:
- Writing **only the name of a street** shows, at the bottom of the results, a row for streets with accidents, with the number of accidents, the fatal ones and, for the most dangerous, the place in the ranking («#[n] among the most dangerous»). A click sets the accident filter on that street, turns the layer on and frames the road.
- Writing the word **“incidente”** or **“sinistro”** (the Italian words for accident; also in the plural) puts the results about accidents **at the top**: the streets and the single accidents. You can add words for the **severity** (“mortale”, “riservata”, “feriti”, “danni/cose”) and a four-digit **year** (for example “incidente mortale roma 2018”). The other words filter by street name.
- Each single accident is a row «Accident [severity] [year]».

titolo: Searching for fires and PAI constraints
parole: fires 2023, PAI constraints, search by year, search by theme, fire location, burnt areas, wildfire.
domande: How do I search for the fires of a year?
How do I find a PAI constraint?
testo:
- **Fires**: writing “incendi” (the Italian word for fires) shows «Fires — all years» with the number of areas burnt by fire and the most recent years (up to three rows). Adding a year (“incendi 2023”) shows the row for that year. A click turns the layer on, filters by year and frames the city (zoom 12). You can also search the **locations** of the fires already loaded in the tiles.
- **PAI constraints**: the search proposes the PAI themes and their classes; a click turns on the corresponding layer.

parole: filters, filters panel, district, neighbourhood, UPL, line, year, severity, parcel, sheet, number, filter chips, mask, area filter, cadastre.
domande: How do I limit the map to a neighbourhood?
How do I filter a transport line?
How do I filter accidents by year?
testo:
The **Filters** tab of the left-hand bar (on a smartphone in the «Layers» sheet) gathers four filters. A number on the tab says how many are active; under the search field the **chips** of the filters appear, each with a ✕ to remove it.

1. **Area: district › neighbourhood › UPL.** These are three cascading menus: choosing a level narrows the list of the next level, and choosing a low level also sets its parents. The entries are «— All —» and the areas; the districts have the full name (I · Centro Storico, II · Brancaccio, III · Oreto, IV · Mezzomonreale, V · Noce, VI · Resuttana, VII · Mondello, VIII · Libertà). The map **frames the area** and **lightens everything else** with a mask, for all layers. Removing a level also removes those below it; the level above stays.
2. **Public transport line.** It restricts routes and stops to a single line (and to the stops where it passes). The list has one entry per line (the two directions joined): first the buses, then the trams, then the railway; the numbers in numerical order.
3. **Accidents: year and severity.** «All years» or one of 2015, 2016, 2017, 2018, 2020, 2021, 2022, 2023 (2019 is not in the dataset); the severity is «All», Fatal, Injured with guarded prognosis, With injuries, Property damage only. They combine in AND with the **street** chosen from the search. When a filter is active the accidents layer turns on by itself and the points are visible from zoom 12 (otherwise from zoom 14). Chips: «Accidents [year]», «Accidents [severity]», «Accidents: [street]».
4. **Cadastral parcel: sheet and number.** Two fields and a button. Both are needed («Enter both the sheet and the parcel»), the zoom must be at least 12 («Move closer to the area (zoom 12 or more) and try again») and the parcel is found **only if its tiles are already loaded**: if it does not find it, it says «No parcel found: move the map to the right area and try again». If it finds it, it turns on the cadastre, highlights it, frames it and shows a box «Searched parcel — Sheet [n] · Parcel [n]».

The chosen filters are also included in the link of «Share this view».

parole: reset, restore settings, customisations, layer order, initial prompt, undo my changes, default colours.
domande: How do I reset the colours and the order I chose?
What does the button next to the search delete?

titolo: The layers bar and its tabs
parole: layers bar, Layers tab, Basemap, RNDT, My layers, Filters, groups of layers, sections, turn on a layer, eye, switch, left-hand bar.
domande: How do I turn on a layer?
Where do I find the groups?
What are the numbers on the Layers tab?
testo:
The vertical bar on the left has five tabs: **Basemap**, **Layers**, **RNDT**, **My layers** and **Filters**. Only these have a tab of their own; all the other groups of layers (Boundaries, Buildings, Monuments, PAI plan, Population, Terrain, Roadside services, Road safety, Territory, Transport) are **sections of the Layers tab**. The sections are in **alphabetical order** (ignoring capital letters and accents), including those that arrive later; each one opens and closes with a click on the title and the choice is remembered in the browser. Inside a section the subgroup titles (for example «Charging points» in «Roadside services») are collapsible in their turn; once a title is closed, the layers under it are hidden, and a closed section also hides its subgroups.

Each layer has an **eye switch** (the box is there, but the icon is what you see) to turn it on or off. The Layers tab shows whether there are layers on and how many. A click on the active tab folds the panel; the panel stays open until the tab is pressed again or Esc.

If a layer fails to load, a notice «Layer not loaded: [name]» (or «[n] layers not loaded: data unreachable») appears for a few seconds, which is closed with the X.

titolo: The buttons next to a layer
parole: move up and down, zoom to, palette, colours, opacity, slider, centre on the layer, transparency, drawing order.
domande: How do I frame the data of a layer?
How do I make a layer transparent?
testo:
Next to each layer (when needed) there are:
- **Move up / Move down** to change the drawing order.
- **«Zoom to [name]»**: frames the map on the area of the layer's data (the extent of its sources, restricted to the working area).
- **Palette** («Colours of [name]»): see `38-tema-dell-interfaccia.md`.
- **Opacity**: a slider «Opacity of [name]» that **multiplies the original opacity** of all the sub-layers of the layer (fills, lines, points, images, icons and texts). Bringing it back to the maximum restores the original values. The chosen opacity is included in the link of «Share this view».

parole: search layer, filter the list, tooltips on the map, legends on the map, information overlays, find a layer.
domande: How do I find a layer among many?
How do I turn off the tooltips?
Where did the legends go?
testo:
The field **«Search layer…»** filters the list; while the search is in progress nothing stays hidden in closed subgroups, so the layer found can be seen.

Below there is the **«Information overlays»** menu with two switches:
- **«Map tooltips»**: the tooltip with the main data when the mouse passes over.
- **«Legends on the map»**: if on, all the legends stay on the map; if off, each legend moves **under its own layer** in the Layers panel, as in GIS programs.

parole: legend, filter from the legend, collapse, legend entry, only this one, second click, all entries, OMI zones, multiple selection.
domande: How do I filter from the legend?
How do I hide the legends?
What happens if I click an entry?
testo:
The legends are in the box at the bottom left; the **«▾ Collapse»** button folds it and reopens it. A legend appears only when its layer is on. Many legend entries are also **filters**, with a box next to the symbol (all on at the start):
- A click on an entry leaves **only that one** on the map; if it was already the only one on, a second click turns all of them on again. The click does not turn off an entry on its own: to see two or more you first choose “only this one” and then turn on the others.
- In legends with many entries (such as the OMI zones) the filter is **multiple selection**: with everything on, the click on an entry (or on a band) leaves on only those; then each click adds or removes them; if nothing is left, everything goes back on.
- Some entries coincide with a whole layer: the box turns the layer on and off.

The legends of the **theme by attribute**, of the **selection on the map** and of the **external services** always stay on the map. Those of the external services say «Loading legend…» or «Legend not available» or «Layer colour» (for vector layers) / «Uploaded file».

titolo: Chips of the active layers and counter
parole: chip, active layers, turn off from the chip, layer counter, dot on the tab.
domande: How do I see which layers are on?
How do I quickly turn one off?
testo: At the top of the map the **chips** of the layers that are on appear (at most 4, then «+[n]»): a click on a chip turns the layer off («Turn off: [name]»). On a smartphone the number of layers that are on appears on the «Layers» button and a dot on the tab.

parole: layer order on the map, above, below, drag, reset order, collapse all, expand all, reorder layers, reorder.
domande: How do I bring a layer above another?
Can I reorder layers from different groups?
testo: At the top of the Layers tab the card **«Layer order on the map»** lists all the layers that are on, of any group: «Top = above on the map. Applies to all active layers, even from different groups.» At least two layers are needed («Turn on at least two layers to change the order»). Each row has **«Move up [name]»**, **«Move down [name]»** and the handle **«Drag to move»**. «Reset order» brings back the starting order. The chosen order is saved in the browser. It also applies to the RNDT layers and «My layers». Inside each group the layers can also be reordered with arrows and dragging; the fixed section titles (such as AMAT and RFI in transport) do not move and the layers are only reordered inside their own section. There are also **«Collapse all»** / **«Expand all»** for the collapsible data under each layer.

parole: zoom, zoom slider, zoom level, from zoom 12, minimum zoom, zoom badge.
domande: How do I change the zoom?
Why does a layer appear only from a certain zoom?
testo: There is a zoom box with a **number** (the current level) and a **slider** from 12 to 18 in steps of 0.1. Many layers have a minimum level and say so in the name, for example «Cadastre: parcels (from zoom 12)», «Street numbers (from zoom 14)», «Accidents (from zoom 14)»: below that level they cannot be seen.

titolo: Right-hand panels and use on a smartphone
parole: right-hand bar, rail, profile, RNDT, Geoimage, Theme, bottom tabs, sheet, Map Layers Add Menu, mobile, phone.
domande: How do the right-hand panels alternate?
How does the bar work on a phone?
testo:
**Right-hand bar.** It has one tab per panel: **Profile**, **RNDT**, **Geoimage**, **Theme**. Only one panel opens at a time; clicking the active tab folds the panel and only the bar remains. When there is no profile open the Profile tab says «Profile: tap the map to open it».

**Smartphone** (up to 720 px). A bar with four tabs at the bottom: **Map** (closes everything), **Layers** (bases, layers, filters), **Add** (My layers, RNDT catalogue, Geoimage) and **Menu** (guides and pages about the project). Only one sheet opens at a time. The pop-up menu closes by touching the map or with Esc. If the window widens beyond 720 px the sheet closes and the interface with side bars returns.

titolo: The selection on the map after a click
parole: selection on the map, highlighting, highlighted areas, selection legend, building, parcel, PRG zone, OMI zone, nearby stop, legend entries, coloured areas.
domande: What are the coloured areas that appear after a click?
How do I remove some of them?
Why do I sometimes see only the building?
testo:
After a click on the map the **areas the data of the profile come from** are highlighted. Each type of highlighted thing has a **label** (the same as in the profile) and a **colour**. The possible labels are: Building, Cadastral parcel, PRG zone, PRG historic net, PRG historic centre, PRG constraint (area), PRG constraint (line), OMI zone, Street number, Municipal property, Census section, Terrain grid point (50 m), Monument, School or nursery, Polling station, Municipal offices, Monumental tree, Drinking fountain, Charging point, Fuel station, Stop, Station, Line, Public work and others.

**What is highlighted.** Only one thing is highlighted: the **building** if the click falls on a building (for monuments, schools and polling stations the polygon of the matching building), the **point** if it falls outside the built-up area. If there is neither (for example with only the cadastre or the PRG on) all the areas stay highlighted. The terrain grid does not count.

**The «Selection on the map» legend.** It appears as long as there is a selection on the map. It has one entry for each label with the colour it is drawn in (a circle or the silhouette of the icon for points, a square for areas). Like the other legends it works as a **filter**: a click on an entry leaves only that one on the map, a second click turns them all on again. The selection is removed with **Esc** or with the «Reset» button next to the search (see `44-ricerca-e-filtri.md`).

**Icons instead of circles.** The point layers with an icon of their own (schools, polling stations, fuel stations, charging points, drinking fountains, trees, monuments, MEF, PEBA and others) are highlighted with the **silhouette of their icon**; the layers without an icon (such as the street numbers) stay circles. The nearby stops are a disc in the colour of the source with the white icon, to tell them apart from the stops of a route. Where two icons touch, one remains, and the nearby stops take precedence.

titolo: Tooltips when the mouse passes over
parole: tooltip, hover, mouse over, details, hide the tooltips, a single tooltip, hover details, pop-up.
domande: How do I turn off the tooltips?
Why do I see only one with several sections?
testo:
On the map there is **a single tooltip**: at every movement of the mouse each module (boundaries, transport, road safety, layers with a popup template…) says what is under the cursor and the content of all of them ends up in a single box, one section under the other, so the tooltips never overlap. The tooltip shows the title in bold (with a coloured dot if needed), a possible badge and the subtitle; for layers with a legend attribute the same symbol as the legend also appears. The search is only made in the layers that are **on**. A 3D object above the map (such as the building by floors) can hide the other sections.

On the areas highlighted after a click the tooltip gives **the name of the layer and the datum that identifies the element** (for example sheet and parcel, PRG zone with description, OMI band, address of the property, street number, name of the stop, census section).

To turn the tooltips on and off there are two controls:
- the switch **«Map tooltips»** in the «Information overlays» menu (see `45-barra-strati-legende-e-ordine.md`);
- the **tooltip button** in the «Selection on the map» legend (only for the tooltips of the highlighted areas): «Hover details: on (click to hide them)» / «Hover details: off (click to show them)».

The tooltip also appears above the stack in the «3D layers» view (see `39-strati-in-3d.md`).

titolo: The radius of nearby points and the dashed circle
parole: radius, nearby points, around the click, metres, radius slider, dashed circle, 300 metres, nearby fuel stations, nearby stops, distance.
domande: Within what distance does it look for nearby points?
How do I change the radius?
What is the dashed circle?
testo:
When you click on the map the profile also shows the **points near** the click (stops, fuel stations, charging points and the other point layers). The **radius** is a single one for all the layers and can be adjusted from the legend: in the «Selection on the map» box there is a slider with the label **«Radius around the click: [n] m»**, from **100 to 500 metres** in steps of 50; at the start it is **300 metres**. The choice stays saved in the browser.

The switch **«Show the circle on the map»** (on at the start) draws a **dashed circle** of the radius around the clicked point, with a light halo under the dark line so that it can be read on any background. Changing the radius or the switch redoes the open profile immediately and the circle updates in real time.

parole: basemap, background map, change the background, satellite, dark map, OpenStreetMap, Esri, Google, white background, thumbnail, base layer, aerial imagery.
domande: How do I change the background map?
How do I see the satellite?
Which base is active at the start?
testo:
The **Basemap** tab (left-hand bar) chooses the map that lies under the layers. **Only one base is visible at a time**; at the start it is «Light map». Each base has a thumbnail and a name; under the list there is the hint «Select the cartography to use as the base.» The bases are divided into groups, as in the selector of the Historical Atlas:

- **Street maps**: Light map (OpenFreeMap), Dark (OpenFreeMap), Bright (OpenFreeMap Bright), OpenStreetMap (standard), OSM France, OSM Humanitarian, Esri Streets (World Street Map), Google (streets), Esri Dark (Dark Gray Canvas).
- **Aerial imagery**: Satellite (Google), Esri (World Imagery), Hybrid (Google satellite with streets and names).
- **Topographic**: Terrain (Google, relief), OpenTopo (contour lines), Esri Topo (World Topographic Map).
- **Historical maps**: see below.
- **Technical cartography**: CSG 1989 (Municipal Technical Map CSG 2k, 1989/91), CTC 2k (Municipal Technical Map, 2007/09), CTR 10k (Regional Technical Map, 2012/13).
- **Neutral background**: Grey (Esri Light Gray Canvas) and White.

The chosen base is included in the link of «Share this view». The button with the moon switches the light/dark theme and the basemap changes accordingly (see `38-tema-dell-interfaccia.md`). In the «3D layers» view the base always takes the lowest plane.

parole: historical maps, old maps, Atlas of historical technical maps, 1580, 1754, 1860, 1877, 1882, 1891, 1893, 1908, 1935, 1941, 1943, 1956, 1962, 1987, 1993, accuracy, georeferenced, Map Warper.
domande: Are there historical maps of Palermo?
What does the green, yellow or red dot mean?
Up to what zoom can they be seen?
testo:
The **«Historical maps»** group (between Topographic and Technical cartography) contains **fifteen maps of Palermo**, from 1580 to 1993, taken from the **Atlas of historical technical maps of Palermo** (OpenDataSicilia), georeferenced on Map Warper. They are chosen like any other base. The years are: 1580, 1754, 1860, 1877, 1882, 1891, 1893, 1908, 1935, 1941, 1943, 1956, 1962, 1987, 1993. Passing the mouse over a map shows the title with the original source and «(overlay accuracy: [high/medium/low])».

**The coloured dot** says how reliable the overlay with today's city is: **green high, yellow medium, red low**. It is an editorial judgement of the atlas: *high* for the aerial photogrammetric surveys (1935, 1956, 1962, 1987, 1993), *medium* for the maps before aerial photogrammetry (1877, 1882, 1891, 1893, 1908, 1941, 1943), *low* for the engravings (1580, 1754, 1860).

**Maximum zoom.** Each map has a maximum zoom (from 16 to 18; the 1893 map goes up to 16).

Above the list a note refers to the Atlas: «Georeferenced maps from the Atlas of historical technical maps (OpenDataSicilia)». The **«Open the Historical Atlas of Palermo»** button opens the complete atlas in a new tab, already positioned on the area (zoom and coordinates) you are looking at; the hint speaks of «overlays, slider comparison and historical postcards».

To **compare** a map with today's city on the map, Geoimage is used (see `50-geoimage.md`). The original sources of the maps (BnF Gallica, Library of Congress, Harvard Map Collection, U.S. Army Map Service, Wisconsin-Milwaukee University, Comune di Palermo) are indicated in the attribution of each map.

parole: My layers, add data, add a service, tree, QGIS Browser, layers on the map, files and services, my own layers, upload.
domande: How do I add my own layer?
Where do I see the layers I have added?
How does the tree work?
testo:
The **My layers** tab (on a smartphone, in the «Add» tab) works like the QGIS Browser. At the top there is a **tree** with a search field (**«Search data sources…»**, which searches by name or address among the saved services) and two branches: **«My data»** (files) and **«Services»**. Below the tree there is **«Layers on the map»**, the list of the layers that were added, each with its checkbox, its opacity and the arrows for the order; if there are none it says «No layers on the map: load a file or add a service from the tree above.» The tree is built only once: open branches and typed text stay even when the group is redrawn.

The description of the group: «Files loaded from your computer and XYZ, WMS and WFS services added by address, also restored from the saved state.»

The layers that were added also appear in the data table (see `40-tabella-dei-dati-ed-esportazione.md`) and in the stack of layers in 3D as «Other layers». Only the ones that can be reopened from a public address go into the «Share this view» link (see `43-condividi.md`).

titolo: My data: files from the computer and from a web address
parole: load file, GeoJSON, KML, KMZ, GPX, Shapefile, zip, CSV, latitude longitude, Google Sheets, https address, shared sheet, upload a file, formats.
domande: Which formats can I load?
How do I load a Google sheet?
Why do I only see part of the file?
testo:
Formats: **GeoJSON, KML/KMZ, GPX, Shapefile (.zip) and CSV with latitude and longitude**.
- **«Load a file from your computer»**: you choose the file. The app reads it and converts it to GeoJSON in WGS84; if there are errors it shows them («Not loading “[file]”: [reason]»). A Shapefile goes in a zip file that also contains the .prj file; GeoJSON and CSV must be in WGS84.
- **«From a web address (https)»**: you paste an https address («Paste an https address.») and press **Load**. The file is downloaded through the app's proxy. The file is a copy that does not update by itself; maximum 10 MB.
- **Google Sheets sheet**: it must be shared first: «In Share → General access choose “Anyone with the link” with the Viewer role. The sheet becomes a CSV (only the sheet indicated in the link) and must have lat and lon columns. Maximum 10 MB.»

Of each file only the features **inside the municipality of Palermo** are kept. A layer from a file is saved in the browser (up to 5 MB); beyond that, it only lasts while the page is open and next to the name «this session only» appears. The data of the files stay in the browser: they are not sent to anyone.

titolo: Services: XYZ, WMS, WMTS, WFS and ArcGIS REST
parole: service, XYZ, WMS, WMTS, WFS, ArcGIS REST, MapServer, FeatureServer, capabilities, read the service, data or images, token, user, password, add a WMS.
domande: How do I add a WMS service?
What does «Show as» mean?
Where do I enter user and password?
testo:
The **Services** branch has a sub-branch for each type: **XYZ, WMS, WMTS, WFS and ArcGIS REST**. The **«+»** button («Add a [type] service») opens a form:
- **Name (optional)** («What do you call it»).
- **Service address**: for XYZ an address with `{z}/{x}/{y}`; for ArcGIS REST the address of a MapServer or FeatureServer (with `?token=…` if needed); for the others the address of the service. The app's proxy only accepts **https** addresses.
- **User (if needed)** and **Password (if needed)**: the password stays «only while the page is open».
- For ArcGIS, a **Service token** field.
- **Read the service** («Reading the service…»): reads the list of layers and the choice to be made: you tick the layers and press **«Add selected»** («Choose at least one item.» if nothing is selected). If the service has a tile cache, a single layer with all the levels is added as «Images».
- **Show as**: **«Data (features you can query)»** or **«Images (like a map)»**, when the service allows both.

Some services are not supported: «(not supported: EPSG:3857 required)» and, for WMTS, «(not supported: EPSG:3857 and 256 px tiles required)». Errors appear as «Unable to read the service: [reason]» or «Unable to load: [reason].» At the end: «Added to the map.»

parole: saved services, 50 services, padlock, password required, bin, remember the service, token, credentials, limit.
domande: Do the services stay saved?
Is the password saved?
How many services can I save?
testo:
The services that were added stay **saved in the browser** (only the address and the choices, never the data) **up to 50**; beyond the limit the service goes on the map but is not saved («Added to the map. You have reached the limit of [n] saved services: this one will not be saved.»). A click on a saved service puts it back on the map as it was, without reading the capabilities again; the bin removes it from the list.

**Credentials.** User and password are kept **only in memory, for the session**: never in localStorage, IndexedDB or in the address. Of the service the user name is remembered, never the password. When it is reopened the service shows a **padlock** and its layer does not start until the password is entered again («Password for “[user]” required — [url]»); for a service with a token «Token required — [url]» appears. Each site has its own access header and goes through the proxy.

titolo: Ready-made lists: orthophotos, Esri bases, the City's historical maps, cultural heritage
parole: orthophoto, Regione Siciliana, Esri, Sispi historical maps, SAS 1981, cultural heritage, archaeological sites, archaeological parks, ready to switch on, aerial images, geological maps.
domande: Are there ready-made services?
Where do I find the orthophotos?
testo:
In the Services branch there are groups of ready-made services: one click puts them on the map (the tiles only start loading then, and only for the area in view).
- **Regione Siciliana - Ortofoto**: aerial images placed **under the data**, with the layers on top. Among the entries: Ortofoto 2022 (20 cm), 2019 (20 cm, AGEA), 2013 (15 cm for Enna, Messina, Palermo, Ragusa, Trapani; 25 cm), 2008 (25 cm).
- **Esri - Basi cartografiche**: Esri street and topographic bases, placed under the data (among the entries Esri Standard and Esri Topo).
- **Comune di Palermo - Carte storiche**: historical maps, surveys and orthophotos of the City (Sispi), for example SAS 1981 (historic centre, roof map), Ortofoto del centro storico 2000, Carta tecnica comunale 1989-91, SAS 1973 (spot-height plan).
- **Regione Siciliana - Beni culturali**: cultural heritage services (SITR) put on the map as **queryable data** over the area of Palermo, for example Beni isolati, Beni paesaggistici (D.Lgs. 42/04), Parchi archeologici (2016), Siti archeologici.

- **ISPRA - Carte geologiche**: geological map 1:50,000 (raster) and the 1:25,000 survey data of the Geological Survey of Italy (CARG): geological units, Quaternary deposits, boundaries, tectonic and structural elements, bedding attitudes, resources and prospecting (quarries, springs, wells, boreholes), put on the map as WMS under the data. The 1:25,000 geomorphology is not included: the service no longer appears to be active.

A few XYZ services, the WMS of the City of Palermo (Sispi) and the ArcGIS REST services of the SITR of the Regione Siciliana are also already loaded, as examples.

titolo: What the RNDT catalogue is and how to open it
parole: RNDT, catalogue, National Register of Territorial Data, openrndt-geolibre plugin, Andrea Borruso, onData, search for data, add data from the catalogue, spatial data catalog.
domande: What is the RNDT catalogue?
How do I open it?
Who wrote the plugin?
testo:
The **«RNDT catalogue: add data to the map»** button (icon of the two layers) in the toolbar at the top right opens the catalogue of the **Repertorio Nazionale dei Dati Territoriali** (National Register of Territorial Data): the list of the geographic data published by bodies all over Italy. The title of the panel is **«RNDT catalogue · Palermo»**. The panel sits alongside the place profile in the right-hand bar (on a smartphone it overlays the bottom sheet) and the **RNDT** tab switches from the catalogue to the profile. While it loads it says «Loading the catalogue…». It is closed with «Close the RNDT catalogue» or with **Esc**: the first Esc closes the catalogue, the second the profile.

The catalogue is based entirely on the **openrndt-geolibre** plugin, conceived and written by **Andrea Borruso (onData)**, MIT licence; in the panel «openrndt-geolibre plugin by …» appears. The project only adapted it (the plugin is loaded only on first use and an Italian translation of it exists). The «RNDT plugin» page of the menu explains how to use it and gives the credit.

parole: search the catalogue, topic, body, WMS, WFS, Palermo boundary, download, features outside the municipality, find data.
domande: How do I search for a dataset?
Why do I only see Palermo?
What happens to the data outside the municipality?
testo:
You search by **text, topic or body**, always within the **area of Palermo**: «Downloads are always limited to the Palermo area». The plugin's search controls are limited by the app to that area. A **WMS** service is added as a layer of images; a **WFS** service as geographic features that can be queried.

The data that are downloaded are filtered on the municipality of Palermo: the app keeps the whole features that touch the municipality (without cutting them), and warns when it discards some: «“[name]”: [n] features out of [tot] are outside the municipality of Palermo and are not shown.» For files with rows without coordinates it says «[n] rows without valid coordinates were skipped».

Access to the external service goes through a **Worker proxy** of the app: in production the address is fixed (a link with a different proxy cannot send users' data to someone else's proxy).

titolo: The «RNDT» group in the layers bar
parole: RNDT group, layers added from the catalogue, remove, switch on, this session only, saving, restore.
domande: Where do I find the layers I added from the catalogue?
How do I remove them?
Do they stay when I reopen?
testo:
The layers that were added appear in the **«RNDT»** group (RNDT tab of the left-hand bar) and among the **Topics**. The group explains: «Data added from the RNDT catalogue, also restored from the saved state. They are added from the catalogue button in the toolbar.» and, if it is empty: «No RNDT layers: look for one in the catalogue.» There is the **«＋ From the RNDT catalogue»** button. Each layer has: the **eye** to switch it on and off, the **opacity** slider, the bin **«Remove layer [name]»**, and the arrows for the order (see `45-barra-strati-legende-e-ordine.md`). The layers are in **alphabetical order**; a dot appears with the count of the layers that are on.

The layers are **saved by themselves** in the browser and come back when it is reopened, on or off as they were. A layer whose address is known is saved with the address; data with no known address are saved in the browser up to **5 MB per layer**: beyond that, or if the browser blocks the storage, they last for the session and a notice says so. Next to the name, **«(this session only)»** warns that the layer could not be saved (for example because «“[name]” is too large to be saved»); **«(loading errors)»** and **«(unavailable)»** signal problems.

titolo: Querying the RNDT layers: profile, tooltips and legends
parole: Other data (RNDT), GetFeatureInfo, attributes, query a WMS, remote tooltip, service legend, GetLegendGraphic, popup, feature information.
domande: How do I see the information of an RNDT layer?
Why does the WMS not show me attributes?
Where do I find the legend?
testo:
- **Profile**: a click on the map queries the RNDT layers (and those of «My layers») that are on. The answers are in the **«Other data (RNDT)»** tab, with a box for each layer and the source indicated («Source: [host] (RNDT catalogue)»). For **WFS** the profile shows the attributes of the clicked feature (you have to click right on the feature); for **WMS** the app asks the service for the information on the point (`GetFeatureInfo`, on a window of ±50 pixels around the click) and reports the answer; for **ArcGIS** it runs a query on the point. If the level is graphic only it says so. The data of external services are for information only.
- **Tooltips**: the **vector** layers that were added show, when the mouse passes over them, the name, the first property with the layer's colour and a couple of lines. For **WMS and image-based ArcGIS** services the request to the server only starts when the mouse stops (otherwise every movement would be a request). The extents of the catalogue data appear in the map's single tooltip, from the smallest to the largest.
- **Legends**: one block for each layer that is on. For WMS it is the service's `GetLegendGraphic` image; for ArcGIS MapServer the classes with their symbol; for vector data a small square of the colour with which they are drawn. XYZ and WMTS have no legend. If the service does not answer it says «Legend not available» and does not retry at every click.

titolo: What Geoimage is and how to open it
parole: Geoimage, historical map, georeference, overlay an image, GCP, control points, ground control points, opacity, Geoimage tab, old map.
domande: What is Geoimage?
How do I overlay an old map on today's city?
Which images can I use?
testo: **Geoimage · historical maps** lets you overlay a historical map (or any image) on modern cartography and **georeference** it, that is, associate real geographic coordinates with it through **Ground Control Points (GCP)**. In the Digital Twin it works on the Palermo basemap. The idea and the code come from Geoimage by @gbvitrano (ported to MapLibre). It opens from the **Geoimage** tab of the right-hand bar (on a smartphone from the button in the «Layers»/«Add» sheet) and closes with «Close Geoimage» (on a smartphone with the X at the top right of the panel). At the start the panel says «Load a historical image to get started.» The complete guide is also on the «Geoimage guide» page of the menu.

parole: load historical map, JPG PNG WEBP BMP, drag, handles, scale, distort, rotate, lock, reset, undo, redo, upload image.
domande: How do I load the image?
What do the handles do?
Can I undo a move?
testo:
1. **Frame the area** with the app's search (street, house number, district), so that the image loads already close to the right place.
2. **Load**: you drag the file (**JPG, PNG, WEBP, BMP**) into the **«Load historical map»** box or you click the box to choose the file. The image appears in the centre of the map with the handles and follows the map even if it is rotated or tilted in 3D. The panel says «Image loaded. Position it with the handles on the map, then add the GCPs (G key).»
3. **Position and orient** with the handles on the map: the **orange circle in the centre** moves the image; the **circle with the arrow above the north side** rotates it; the **handles at the corners** have two modes that are switched with the **«Handles: scale / distort»** button: in *scale* (orange squares) they resize in proportion keeping the opposite corner fixed; in *distort* (blue diamonds) each corner moves freely, useful for historical maps that are not rectangular.
4. In the **«Position overlay»** section there are the precise controls: arrows to move, rotation of 5° left and right, scale 10 % up or down, ⌖ to frame the image, **«Lock (L)»** to freeze the handles and **Reset** to bring everything back to the initial position.
5. **Undo** (Ctrl+Z) and **Redo** (Ctrl+Y) go back and forth through up to **50 positions**; with Shift they take 10 steps. The history starts again when another image is loaded. **«Remove image»** takes the image off the map.

If you choose a file that is not an image: «choose an image file (JPG, PNG, WEBP or BMP).»

parole: GCP, add GCP, step 1, step 2, at least 3 points, align image to the GCPs, affine, polynomial, RMSE, residual, error in metres, georeferencing.
domande: How do I add a GCP?
How many are needed?
What does RMSE mean?
testo:
**Adding a GCP** (button **«Add GCP (G)»** or the G key): for each point you need **two clicks on the map**.
- **Step 1**, on the historical image: you click a recognisable point (a crossroads, a building, a monument); an orange circle appears.
- **Step 2**, on the base map: you click the same place in the modern cartography; the GCP is added and the circle becomes red and numbered.
- **Swipe** or **Spotlight** help you see the base under the image to click precisely.
- **Esc** cancels the pending step 1; pressed again it leaves GCP mode. In this mode clicks on the map do not open the place profile.
- You need **at least 3 GCPs**, preferably spread over the corners of the area covered by the image. With fewer the panel says «[n] GCPs: at least [min] needed».
- A table shows for each GCP its coordinates, pixel and residual; **«Remove GCP [n]»** removes one point and **«Delete all GCPs»** removes them all. **Delete** or **Backspace** removes the last one added.

**Aligning.** With 3 or more GCPs **«Align image to the GCPs»** is enabled, which moves the image to the calculated coordinates. The **«Transformation»** menu chooses the type: **Affine (≥3 GCP)** or **Polynomial 2 (≥6 GCP)**. You can repeat it by adding more GCPs.

**Checking the error (RMSE).** As soon as there are enough GCPs for the chosen transformation the **RMSE** appears, the mean error in **metres**: the lower it is, the better. In the table each GCP has its own **residual in metres**, coloured relative to the average: **green** if it is within the norm, **orange** if it is high, **red** if it is much higher than the others. If the error is high you reposition the least precise GCPs (by dragging them on the map) or add more.

parole: swipe, spotlight, radius, invert, comparison, opacity, sliding line, circle, compare maps.
domande: How do I compare the historical map with today's?
How do I use Spotlight?
testo:
In the **«Visual comparison»** section:
- **Swipe**: splits the map with a **sliding vertical line** (on the left the historical image, on the right the modern base alone). You drag the central handle between 2 % and 98 % of the width; with Swipe on you can still move and zoom the map by keeping the cursor away from the handle.
- **Spotlight**: a **circle that follows the mouse** reveals the modern base under the image. The **«Radius»** slider enlarges or reduces the circle; the **⇄** button inverts the effect (the image is only seen inside the circle).
- Swipe and Spotlight **are mutually exclusive**: turning one on turns the other off. Pressing the same button again turns it off.
- A slider adjusts the **opacity** of the image; the image sits above all the layers.

parole: export, KMZ, GeoTIFF, QGIS, .points, world file, GCP GeoJSON, JSON, project, autosave, MapWarper, save.
domande: How do I bring the result into QGIS?
Is the work saved?
Can I reopen it?
testo:
In the **Export** section:
- **KMZ**: for Google Earth, QGIS and ArcGIS, with the image embedded.
- **GeoTIFF**: a raster with the coordinates embedded, for QGIS, ArcGIS, GDAL. The button opens **«GeoTIFF settings»**: **coordinate reference system** (WGS 84, UTM 32N or 33N, Web Mercator), **resampling** (Nearest neighbour or Bilinear (2×2)), **maximum resolution** (long side) and **compression** (None or **LZW (recommended)**), then «Export GeoTIFF». In EPSG:4326 with the affine transformation is embedded without resampling. At least the number of GCPs required by the transformation is needed.
- **GCP for QGIS (.points)**: the GCPs for the QGIS Georeferencer.
- **World file**: the affine transformation in six lines (at least 3 non-collinear GCPs are needed).
- **GCP GeoJSON**: the control points as geographic data.
- **JSON** («Export JSON» and «Import JSON»): saves and reopens the whole project (image, position and GCPs); it is the same format as Geoimage.

**Saving.** The project is saved **by itself in the browser**: when you reload the page you find the image where it was (if the browser allows it; with large images or with the storage blocked Geoimage warns you and recommends «Export JSON»). **Ctrl+S** saves by hand in the browser («Project saved in this browser.»).

**Shortcuts** (with the panel open and the cursor outside the text fields): **G** GCP mode; **Esc** cancels step 1, then leaves GCP mode; **Delete/Backspace** removes the last GCP; **Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Y** undo and redo; **Ctrl+S** save; **L** locks or unlocks the handles.

**What changes in the Digital Twin compared with the original Geoimage**: the image sits above all the layers; it also works with the map tilted and rotated; the basemap and the search are those of the Digital Twin (there is no base selector or place search of Geoimage); the handles are only visible with the panel open; switching scale/distort is done with a button (a click on the map opens the profile); it works best with a mouse.

**More precision.** For more precise georeferencing, with advanced polynomial transformations and online collaboration, **MapWarper** (mapwarper.net) is recommended. The already georeferenced historical maps of the Atlas are among the map's bases (see `47-mappe-di-base-e-storiche.md`).

titolo: The top menu and the information pages
parole: menu, pages, Home, Map, Digital Twin, Topics, Guide, Geoimage guide, RNDT plugin, Sources and notes, Privacy, About, Presentation, page index, information pages.
domande: What is in the top menu?
How do I close a page?
Where do I find the sources and the notes?
testo:
The menu is next to the logo and is the same on every page of the site (on a smartphone it is in the «Menu» tab). Its entries are **Home**, **Map**, **Digital Twin**, **General guide** (with **RNDT plugin** and **Geoimage guide** in the drop-down next to it), **Sources and notes** and **About** (with **Presentation** and **Privacy** in the drop-down next to it). The entry of the page you are on is highlighted.

**Home** (`index.html`) is the page where you choose and add the map's layers; the **topic** filter is here. **Map** takes you back to the map.

Digital Twin, Guide, RNDT plugin, Geoimage guide, Sources and notes, About and Privacy are **separate pages** (`digitaltwin.html`, `guida.html`, `plugin.html`, `geoimage.html`, `fonti.html`, `about.html`, `privacy.html`), at **full width**, split into bands, and many have a **side index** («Page index», «Guide index»). To go back to the map, choose **Map** in the menu. From the map, the same entries instead open the information sheets above the map, which close by pressing the entry again or with **Esc**.

- **Digital Twin**: «The city in layers: cadastre, population, buildings, transport, safety and much more.» Sections: «What a Digital Twin means to us, in plain words», «How it is organised», «The sources», «How to use it», «What it is for».
- **Topics**: «What the Digital Twin is about, topic by topic.» A box for each topic, with the description and the list of the layers and the **«Show on the map»** button that switches on the topic's layers and closes the page (off if the layers are not yet available). It is no longer a menu entry: topics are chosen from the Home filter.
- **Guide**: «How to use the map, step by step.» It has two groups, **Features** and **Use cases**, steps with images and video (the video «Palermo Digital Twin: how to use the map with Palermo's open data»).
- **Geoimage guide**: «How to overlay a historical map on the cartography and georeference it.» (see `50-geoimage.md`)
- **RNDT plugin**: explains the RNDT catalogue and gives the credit to Andrea Borruso (see `49-catalogo-rndt.md`), with use cases.
- **Sources and notes**: «Where the data come from and what to keep in mind when using them.» It has the sections **«Data sources»** (one entry per source, with the date, the links to the original data and the licence) and **«Good to know»** (the caveats).
- **Privacy**: see below.
- **About**: «The OpenDataSicilia community, which promotes open data in Sicily.» Sections: What it is, Who we are, Where we are (mailing list, Facebook, Twitter, Telegram, GitHub Discussions), **Contribute and report issues** (the button «Open an issue on GitHub» for errors in the data or ideas), Credits (Development, Tools used). The web app is designed and developed by @gbvitrano in collaboration with Claude AI (Anthropic).

**Presentation.** It is a separate page (`presentazione.html`) with sections such as «Why?», «What you’ll find on the map», «Open data, with sources», «The app tour» (video), «Works on smartphones and tablets too», «All the layers, in 3D» (see `39-strati-in-3d.md`) and «Contribute and report issues».
